claims.headline: The United States remained the region's population heavyweight.
claims.statement: In 2024, the United States had 340.1M people, compared with 130.9M in Mexico and 41.3M in Canada.
claims.why_it_matters: Scale explains why the United States can dominate regional totals even when a share-based comparison points elsewhere.
claims.visual: Population bars for Canada, Mexico, and the United States.

claims.headline: The United States operated at a much larger GDP scale than its neighbors.
claims.statement: In 2024, the United States posted a GDP of $28.75T, versus $2.24T for Canada and $1.86T for Mexico.
claims.why_it_matters: Business readers need the scale context before they interpret generation totals or policy choices.
claims.visual: GDP comparison bars with all three countries on one axis.

claims.headline: Canada was the clean-share outlier in the latest power mix.
claims.statement: In 2025, clean sources supplied 77.0% of Canada's electricity mix, ahead of the United States at 43.0% and Mexico at 25.9%.
claims.why_it_matters: This is the clearest opening contrast for the package because it names the regional outlier and frames the rest of the comparison.
claims.visual: Clean-share bars for Canada, Mexico, and the United States.

claims.headline: Hydropower remained Canada's largest single source.
claims.statement: Hydropower led Canada's 2025 generation stack at 344.7 TWh, well ahead of gas and wind.
claims.why_it_matters: The Canada angle is stronger when the clean-share lead is grounded in the source that anchors the stack.
claims.visual: Canada source stack with hydropower highlighted.

claims.headline: Mexico remained the gas-heavy outlier in the latest mix.
claims.statement: Gas supplied 61.6% of Mexico's electricity mix in 2025, the highest gas share of the three markets.
claims.why_it_matters: This gives the package a clear counterpoint to Canada's cleaner grid profile.
claims.visual: Mexico generation stack with gas highlighted.

claims.headline: Mexico posted the lowest annual CO2 total in the latest year.
claims.statement: In 2024, Mexico recorded 461.0 Mt of annual CO2 emissions, below Canada's 533.3 Mt and far below the United States at 4904.1 Mt.
claims.why_it_matters: The emissions comparison keeps the package from collapsing into a power-mix story only.
claims.visual: Latest annual CO2 totals for the three countries.

claims.headline: The United States still led the region on clean-power volume.
claims.statement: The United States generated 1,943.6 TWh from clean sources in 2025, the largest absolute clean-power total in this three-country set.
claims.why_it_matters: The U.S. line keeps the package honest: the clean-share lag does not erase the scale of clean generation already on the system.
claims.visual: Absolute clean-generation totals for the three countries.
